Bob / team —

Appreciate the specifics. Below is a single-note proposal that maps to your asks; I kept it example-driven so Procurement and Finance can see cashflow and amortization impact immediately. Priyom added a short resilience clause suggestion for the SLA.

Proposal (example numbers for Helix sizing ~10 reserved nodes + 20% buffer):

Option A — Reserve-first (predictable first-year cashflow)
- Reserved node commit: 10 nodes (dedicated), billed monthly; platform fee amortized over 36 months.
- Platform fee: presented as a single contract line but amortization schedule provided for 36 months to align with Helix capex.
- Migration credit: $45,000 phased over the first 12 months (milestones: pilot completion $15k, data migration acceptance $15k, ops handoff $15k). Credit applies as invoice offsets.
- Elasticity / burst: 2000 token-hours per quarter of burst at no charge ("elasticity credit"); subsequent burst billed at metered rate.
- Support: Silver tier (Mon-Fri 8x5 response with 4-hr P1 SLA) included. 24/7 oncall retainer option available at fixed monthly rate.
- Resilience credit: if sustained node-level unavailability > 6 hours in a month (after failover), Helix receives a pro-rata credit against the platform fee for that month (capped at 10% per month).

Option B — Elasticity-first (lower up-front, more metered)
- Smaller reserved commit: 6 nodes; higher elasticity allowance (5000 token-hours per quarter).
- Platform fee: lower base fee, same amortization disclosure; larger portion of cost shifted to usage.
- Migration credit: $30,000 applied at pilot completion and final cutover.
- Support: includes Bronze tier (business hours) with optional SRE retainer for on-call augmentation.

Why this structure?
- Gives Helix an amortization schedule for accounting purposes while preserving a practical buffer for burst and failover.
- Migration credit tied to milestones reduces risk for Redwood while aligning incentives for rapid acceptance.
- Resilience credit is a new construct we've used for a few customers — it provides a direct economic remedy tied to availability without complicated SLA make-goods.

Attachments & artifacts: I re-attached the FAQ and the short strike-sheet for a quick side-by-side. Priyom will add a short note on the "buffer" architecture and how we measure burst token-hours (so you can map to your telemetry).

Next steps:
- If Procurement confirms capital treatment, we'll produce an invoice schedule + amortization table.
- Marissa will follow up with a commercial term-sheet (amber/redline friendly) and a DocuSign envelope if you want to move to LOI.

Open question for Procurement / Finance (cc'd): do you need the migration credit on the same PO as the platform fee, or can it be handled as a separate credit memo? That dictates how we draft the SOW/payment terms.

Thanks —
Maya
